blockers.summary: The repaired gap-length clause identifies the screen's ten-base-pair criterion with the enzyme's REPORTED REQUIREMENT ("the top of the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to need"). The paper's only source for that range reports 7-10 as OPTIMAL and SIX as necessary, the producing artifact carries the requirement as 5 or 6 and calls 7-10 the optimum, and the manuscript itself says so twice elsewhere. The round-27 repair fixed the arithmetic of the old "more than" and in doing so promoted the mis-description from an incidental phrase into the load-bearing one.
blockers.quote: At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, the top of the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to need, so a shorter run that could still license cleavage goes uncounted and that last figure is a floor; the deposit gives the series.
blockers.evidence: In-paper anchor: the only occurrence of the range is the Introduction, line 88, cited to reference 13 = PMID 24981949; PMID 35664704 (whose 7-10 IS a stated minimum, of RNA:DNA hybridised nucleotides) is cited NOWHERE in the article (grep -c '35664704' on the pinned .md = 0) and is absent from fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md. Source verbatim, research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json records[0] (PMID: 24981949) quotes[0] and quotes[1]: 'gap of six DNA nucleotides is necessary for noteworthy RNase H activity' and 'DNA gap size between 7 and 10 nucleotides is optimal'. Producing artifact, research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json (the file that yields 87/88/87, 190/266/342 and 45.8/33.1/25.4, all of which I re-derived and which check out): thresholds.min_contiguous_dna_nt_for_rnaseh1.values = [5, 6], with _why_two = 'The retrieved sources disagree by one nucleotide and the choice would decide the headline, so both are carried and neither is presented as the answer'; geometries[1].role = 'longer gap, inside the reported optimum' and geometries[2].role = 'longer gap, top of the reported optimum' — the artifact says OPTIMUM at exactly the place the manuscript says NEED. The manuscript contradicts itself in two further places: line 87-88, 'Its length requirement is reported as a DNA gap of at least six nucleotides, with seven to ten the working range'; and Methods line 107-108, on its own 5-6-5 panel, 'That gap is the shortest length the cited source credits rather than its preferred one'. Cross-check that the same repository holds no source calling 7-10 a requirement of the kind cited: lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json also holds 'requires a gap size of at least five' (PMID 39126066), '6-8 nucleotide long DNA oligomer is sufficient' (PMID 26544037), 'internal stretch of at least 6' (PMID 28290206), 'six or more bases' (PMID 41614678).
blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: Two ways. (1) Internal contradiction with consequence: the panel this paper reports is 5-6-5, a six-nucleotide gap. If seven-to-ten is what the enzyme NEEDS, every design in the paper is below the enzyme's requirement — which the Methods explicitly deny. A reader cannot hold both sentences. (2) The clause is the sole justification for the word 'floor', and it sizes that floor. Told the criterion sits at the top of a 7-10 requirement, a reader concludes only runs of seven to nine go uncounted. On the paper's own held sources the reported minimum is five or six, so runs from five upward go uncounted and the undercount behind 25.4% (and behind 45.8%) is materially larger than the sentence implies. The error runs in the direction that flatters the reported rates.
blockers.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md line 219; carried verbatim into fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf, -manuscript.pdf, -preprint.pdf, -anonymized.pdf and -manuscript.docx (all five text layers checked at the pin), and into the published archive at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22182180 (the manifest entry for the .md carries sha256 682025231a3c…, and deposit-state.json published.manifest_digest = a4d4ad6f1ca0… = the pin's archive_content_digest).
blockers.what_a_true_sentence_would_have_to_asser: That at 5-10-5 the whole-gap criterion demands ten paired bases; that ten is the top of the seven-to-ten DNA gap size PMID 24981949 reports as OPTIMAL for a gapmer, and is ABOVE the five-to-six nucleotides the same body of retrieved sources reports as the MINIMUM for cleavage (research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json thresholds.min_contiguous_dna_nt_for_rnaseh1 = [5, 6]); and that it is therefore a run shorter than ten — down to five or six — that could still license cleavage and goes uncounted, so the figure is a floor. The 'floor' direction and the geometry are untouched; what must go is the identification of the criterion with a REQUIREMENT of seven-to-ten, because no source the paper cites states one. Do not repair it by citing PMID 35664704 without also adding it to the reference list and stating that its seven-to-ten is a count of hybridised nucleotides rather than of gap nucleotides — the Introduction, line 89-90, tells the reader those are different units ('a length of hybrid rather than a count of gap nucleotides'), and line 229 repeats it ('These are whole-duplex run lengths rather than the enzyme's own unit').

p1s.summary: The new Introduction clause 'only the first is even partly in silico, pairing complementarity prediction with transcriptomics' is read by no instrument. The one guard at that site binds the NEXT sentence only.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_manuscript_asserts_the_relation_its_artifacts_compute.py row 'in-silico-half-of-the-first-step' anchors on site regex r'This work performs[^;]{0,140};' and forbids only 'all five of those steps|all five steps|each of the five steps|the whole of the first step|the first three steps|steps one to'. The repaired clause sits in the preceding sentence, outside that site. Repository-wide search over non-autonomy code for the clause's content — grep -rn 'partly in silico|even partly|only the first is' over research/, systems/, scripts/ — returns no guard on it (only unrelated prose in other modules). The old wording it replaced ('the first in silico and the rest in the laboratory') was equally unguarded, so this is an inherited hole rather than a new one, but the repair changed what the sentence asserts about a cited source while leaving nothing that reads it.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Rewriting the clause to 'the first two are in silico', 'the first three are computational', or dropping 'only', would silently enlarge what this work is presented as having done within a cited five-step framework, and every gate would stay green: the guarded sentence beside it is unchanged, lint_claims sees no strength word, and the source verbatim in lit-targets-aso-instruments.json is not compared against the prose by anything.

p2s.summary: The repaired Introduction clause asserts that step 1 of the cited workflow is only PARTLY in silico. Neither the source verbatim nor the repository's own record of it says that; the record's own gloss says the opposite.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript line 94: 'set five steps; only the first is even partly in silico, pairing complementarity prediction with transcriptomics.' The committed source record, research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-instruments.json → supplementary_record_2026_08_31_the_five_step_framework_verbatim.record.five_steps_verbatim, reads: '(1) OffT identification throughcomplementarity prediction and transcriptomics analysis, (2) focus on cell types with relevant ONT activity, (3)verification and margin assessment, (4) risk assessment based on the OffT biological role, and (5) management of unavoidable OffTs.' It nowhere characterises any step as in silico or not, and it does not mark any part of step 1 as laboratory work. The same record's what_the_paper_takes_from_it says 'Step 1 is the only in-silico step' — no 'partly'. The replaced wording ('the first in silico and the rest in the laboratory') matched that gloss; the replacement no longer does. 'five steps' and 'complementarity prediction … transcriptomics' both check out against the verbatim. NOTE the direction: transcriptomics analysis of predicted off-targets is ordinarily a computational analysis of existing expression data, and this work performed none — the word 'transcriptomics' occurs exactly once in the manuscript, in this clause, and no passage states that predicted off-targets were not filtered by expression. Calling that half not-in-silico recasts an unperformed computational step as a wet-lab one, which is the self-serving direction. Kept as P2 rather than graded higher because the repository holds only the abstract of PMID 39912803. The one observation that would settle it: the full text's description of step 1, i.e. whether its transcriptomics analysis is a computational analysis of existing datasets. If it is, this clause is wrong and the scope sentence beside it overstates how much of the available in-silico work was done.

leakage: THREE disclosures. (1) A repository-wide `grep -rn 24981949` returned three CONTENT lines from red-team records, which are on the may-not-read list: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-paper-redteam-round8.md line 154 (a P0 about 5-6-5 versus PMID 24981949, stating that a six-nucleotide gap gives incomplete activity and 7-10 is optimal, plus a 16-nt tooling limit) and line 361 (a fragment list: PMID 24981949 'a gap of six DNA nucleotides is necessary'; 28290206 'at least 6'; 41614678 'six or'), and round9.md line 128 (a note that the Methods attribute the geometry and the source is held). The quantity touched is the one REG-28-01 rests on. I re-derived it end to end from the primary held record instead: research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json records[0].quotes (verbatim context strings) and research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json thresholds.min_contiguous_dna_nt_for_rnaseh1, both read at the pin and both quoted in the finding; no red-team line is relied on. Later searches were scoped away from *-redteam*. (2) The same grep listed PATHS under research/autonomy/** (review-seats/*, receipts/*, research-ledger.json). Filenames only; I opened none of them and no quantity was seen. (3) research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py (a test file, not on the may-not-read list) carries a comment block at lines 1010-1059 that summarises what earlier rounds found at this sentence, including that round 27 changed 'more than the seven-to-ten' to 'the top of'. I had already derived that the old phrasing was arithmetically wrong and that the new one is arithmetically right before reading it, and REG-28-01 is a DIFFERENT defect from the one that comment describes — it is about 'need' versus the sources' 'optimal'/'at least six', which that comment does not raise and which the comment itself repeats ('the criterion still demands the most the enzyme is reported to need').
